claims.text: Anthropic signed a 20-year, 401 MW lease in July 2026, and Google holds about 14% of the company.
In August 2025 Fluidstack leased 200 MW there and then another 160 MW, with Google backstopping $3.2B of the lease obligations and taking warrants for about 14% of TeraWulf.
TeraWulf and Fluidstack also formed a joint venture for a 168 MW campus at Abernathy, Texas.
TeraWulf has leased 839 MW of AI capacity and reports about $27B of contracted revenue.

In July 2026 Anthropic signed a 20-year lease for 401 MW of critical IT load at the Justified Data campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, worth about $19B over the initial term, with first capacity due in the second half of 2027.
In the same announcement TeraWulf sold a 50.1% stake in the Abernathy joint venture to a Fluidstack-led group for about $450M.
At Lake Mariner it had 102 MW of revenue-generating IT capacity online by early July 2026 and 336 MW more under construction.
HPC leases brought in $31.9M of Q2 2026 revenue, against $12.8M from mining.
The quarter's $939.9M net loss came mostly from a $755.7M non-cash charge on the Google warrants.
Kentucky regulators approved a 482 MW power agreement for Justified Data in August 2026, and in October TeraWulf raised contracted power at Muskie to 1 GW.
TeraWulf reports a 2.1 GW controlled pipeline, with 737 MW under construction.

It held $3.0B of cash at the end of June 2026 against $2.5B of convertible notes and $3.2B of secured notes at its WULF Compute unit, and its free cash flow over the prior 12 months was negative $1.9B.
Leased capacity = 839 MW (August 2026)
Contracted revenue = About $27B
Anthropic lease = 401 MW, 20 years, about $19B (July 2026)
Revenue-generating IT load = 102 MW (July 2026)
Q2 2026 = Revenue $44.8M, net loss $939.9M

claims.text: Slovak startup planning an AI data center and supercomputer built on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
It has published few details beyond its founding team and a stated NVIDIA supplier agreement.
Tatra Supercompute presents itself as a project to build an AI data center in Slovakia that pairs AI computing with green energy.
Its founders include CEO and COO Peter Novak, a banking and telecom executive who has led data center projects, and president Robert Lesko, who spent 25 years at Morgan Stanley.
The company's website says it has a supplier agreement with NVIDIA for Blackwell GPUs and that the facility will rank among the most powerful supercomputers in the world.
The company says the data center will draw on electricity generated in Slovakia and help build a Slovak AI business ecosystem.
Country = Slovakia
Planned GPUs = NVIDIA Blackwell
CEO and COO = Peter Novak
